prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1129; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received by phone from the claimant, who reports being rear-ended at a traffic light by another vehicle and says they were taken to hospital with a head injury diagnosed as a concussion.
Entry 2: Confirmed the claimant is the named driver on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the collision. Opened the file and assigned it for handling.
Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by a lawyer. They described the same sequence of events they gave at first notice and said they were stopped and wearing a seatbelt when impact occurred.
Entry 4: Obtained the police report. Officers at the scene recorded the claimant as a occupant in the vehicle and noted the rear impact, with the other driver's account matching the claimant's.
Entry 5: Took statements from two witnesses who saw the collision from the adjacent lane. Both describe the vehicle being struck from behind in the way the claimant described.
Entry 6: Received photographs of the vehicle from the claimant and a repair estimate from the body shop. The damage to the rear is mostly consistent with the reported impact speed and direction.
Entry 7: Inspected the vehicle with the shop's assessor. No prior damage was found, and no earlier repairs to the affected areas appear in the vehicle history.
Entry 8: Reviewed the claimant's medical records. The concussion diagnosis fits the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. Treatment continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the treating provider noted follow-up visits.
Entry 9: Asked the claimant about any earlier injuries to the head or neck. The claimant reported none, and no prior injury to the same body area appears in the records obtained so far.
Entry 10: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described and acknowledged responsibility for the rear impact.
Entry 11: Confirmed with the claimant on a second call that the account has stayed the same across every conversation so far. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start date.
Entry 12: Reviewed the file summary. Liability appears clear, the vehicle damage is in line with the reported impact, and the injury claim is proceeding to evaluation of medical treatment costs and lost time.
